subject: Post-demo cost recap + target $/1M ask (Finlytics)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena@finlytics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo cost recap + target $/1M ask (Finlytics)

Hi Lena — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and our asks so we can size a clean commercial for your procurement team.

Key takeaways from today
- Primary workload: contextual search + summarization for customer support transcripts (~95% text gen).
- Expected steady-state volume: 120M tokens / month (peaks to 300M on batch jobs).
- Latency target: 400ms p95 for single-query pipelines.
- Data residency: US only, SOC2 evidence required (we can provide).

Pricing qualification (we discussed ranges on the call) — can you confirm:
1) Target $/1M tokens you consider reasonable for production (ballpark).
2) Monthly committed tokens range you could commit to in an initial 6–12 month term.
3) Any procurement constraints (PO timelines, internal approvals).

For context, we typically provide a cost comparison vs OpenAI/Anthropic and wider open-hosts when we share an initial commercial. If you can reply with a quick confirmation on the three asks above, I’ll follow up with a short unit-cost grid and two recommended pricing bands (conservative + aggressive) for your legal / procurement.

Next steps
- You: confirm target $/1M and commit range (1–2 short bullets).
- Us: send unit_cost_grid.xlsx + short rationale and suggested commercial by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin | Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: unit_cost_grid.xlsx (spreadsheet), ask-rationale.pdf (one-pager)

From: Lena Park <lena@finlytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo cost recap + target $/1M ask (Finlytics)

Hi Marcus — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers below: 

1) Target $/1M tokens: Our internal target for a vendor is $750–900 / 1M tokens for standard gen traffic. For experimental/large-context jobs we accept a higher effective rate.
2) Commit range: We can commit to 100–150M tokens/month to start, with a ramp to 250–300M over 6 months if performance is stable.
3) Procurement notes: Typical SOW + PO process is 4–6 weeks; legal will want explicit data residency + SLA language.

We’d like the unit cost grid and the two bands you mentioned. Also, can you include a simple scenario showing cost per ticket processed (avg tokens per ticket ~2.4k)? That helps our finance team.

Thanks — Lena
Lena Park | Head of Product Operations | Finlytics

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 12:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo cost recap + target $/1M ask (Finlytics)

Marcus / Aisha — attaching two artifacts: unit_cost_grid.xlsx (3-tier band + host comps) and ask-rationale.pdf (1p). Summary notes below for the thread: 

Internal guidance (quick):
- Finlytics stated target band $750–900; given volume profile (100–300M) we can be competitive but need to be mindful of p95 latency SLO.
- Suggested commercial bands to propose in the external deck:
  - Band A (Conservative): $1,050 / 1M tokens — includes higher SLO reserve and dedicated scaling buffer for p95 headroom.
  - Band B (Aggressive): $750 / 1M tokens — assumes 12-month commit at 200M/month and standard shared infra with caching optimizations.
  - Band C (Promo ramp): $500 / 1M (first 3 months) then step to $900 / 1M — for rapid adoption programs; needs exec approval.

Competitive reference points (public/hosted):
- OpenAI (recent list): ~ $1,200 / 1M for high-throughput programmatic usage (estimate, varies by tier).
- Anthropic: ~ $1,100 / 1M (model dependent).
- Large open-host operators (discounted quantized offerings): $600–800 / 1M depending on configuration.

Caveats and rationale:
- Our Band B assumes we can apply prefix caching and KV cache reuse on the 95% repeated-context traffic — reduces effective token costs by ~15–25%.
- Band A includes a 15% equipment/service premium to guarantee the 400ms p95 during peak concurrency.
- Promo band C is intentionally aggressive to help win the deal but requires LOE for monitoring and potential overage mitigation.

I attached the spreadsheet with line-item math, scenario rows (cost per ticket @ 2.4k tokens), and a short sensitivity table. Use these to populate the external follow-up.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: unit_cost_grid.xlsx, ask-rationale.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: two pricing bands + next steps (Finlytics)

Hi Lena — following up with the two bands we discussed. Attached is the short deck + the unit_cost_grid.xlsx we mentioned. TL;DR proposals: 

Option 1 — Conservative (recommended for strict SLOs)- Unit rate: $1,050 / 1M tokens- Commit: 100M / month (12-month term)- Notes: Dedicated burst buffer, guaranteed p95 SLA, standard SOC2 artifacts included.

Option 2 — Growth (cost-efficient, faster ramp)- Unit rate: $750 / 1M tokens- Commit: 200M / month (12-month term) with quarterly usage reviews- Notes: Shared infra, prefix caching applied, automatic fallbacks to a slightly smaller model if we detect quality drops.

Cost-per-ticket example (avg 2.4k tokens):
- Option 1: $1,050 * (2400 / 1,000,000) = ~$2.52 / ticket
- Option 2: $750 * (2400 / 1,000,000) = ~$1.80 / ticket

Next steps
1) Confirm which option aligns best with Finlytics procurement (or tell us a target in $/1M and we’ll produce a redlineable SOW).
2) If Option 2 preferred, we’ll prepare a 12-month SOW + DocuSign link; timeline ~2–3 weeks for signature if internal approvals go smoothly.
3) We can include a 3-month promo ramp (Band C) as a negotiated line item if you want an adoption window.

DocuSign link (draft): https://docusign.redwood.com/envelopes/ABC-1834 (draft, not final)
Drive deck: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cunit-cost-grid

LMK and we’ll move to legal.

Thanks — Marcus
